author: leopoldasch
text:
Most importantly: can we unlock the "test-time compute overhang"?

Per-token, models are quite smart, but they're limited to thinking for a (human-equivalent) of a few minutes only.

What if we can unhobble them to think and work on projects for hours, days, weeks, months? https://t.co/6G4POfwtOu

quoted.text:
And more on algorithmic progress as an unsung hero/central driver of progress here: https://t.co/Vg74SxNlp3

Us failing to protect the algorithmic secrets is the single most likely way in which China is able to stay competitive in the AGI race. https://t.co/sdfPPdoqTp

author: leopoldasch
text:
Automating AI research is all it takes.

Even if they can't make coffee yet or walk around the office, if the AI systems can do ML research on a computer, that would set off extraordinary feedback loops. https://t.co/uPBz831hN7

author: leopoldasch
text:
Models today have a lot of raw intelligence, but they're still incredibly "hobbled".

If we can:
1. Solve the "onboarding problem"
2. Unlock "thinking longer" via a System II outer loop
3. Hook models up to a computer

We could go from chatbots to agents/drop-in remote workers. https://t.co/7YJuZtjqUB

author: leopoldasch
text:
